title: (WAY TL;DR) That is a very long arc from the Apple IIe.
author: Studio_94
selftext:
After 1.5  years of free access (Google, Microsoft, ect.) mail/storage usage in trying to fully design/develop a "WOW Killer"; I have come to the point where I have a solid and achievable Roadmap to producing my first vertical slice. 

My files are all over the place between one drive, g-drive, and too many portable drives I finally broke down and got away from the imagination and had to dive deep into the rabbit hole of back end repository usage and propagation. 

I worked with GPT to come up with the lowest dollar migration solution because I had packed it all in a massive heap in MS OneDrive. 

The stack we ended up building:

MICROSOFT ONEDRIVE

↓

Microsoft Graph API

↓

Android phone

↓

Termux

↓

rclone

↓

S3-compatible transfer

↓

CLOUDFLARE R2

Canonical object storage for the corpus

↓

Cloudflare D1

Searchable metadata / catalog / manifests

↓

Cloudflare Workers

Repository API and controlled programmatic access

↓

Cloudflare Access

Authentication and access control

↓

DS94 repository tools / MCP

↓

ChatGPT Business + future web interfaces

GitHub sits alongside this as the version-controlled home for the Worker/API code and repository infrastructure configuration.

So right now my Android phone is literally acting as the transfer bridge between Microsoft's cloud and Cloudflare's cloud. Once the raw migration is complete, we'll reconcile and verify the corpus, generate full nested human- and machine-readable manifests, populate the metadata catalog, and then start the real work of organizing and exposing the corpus through controlled web/API access.

The important part is that the original files are being preserved first. Organization, classification, deduplication, derived text, search, and cleanup come afterward rather than modifying the source material during migration.

I didn't really hear about this "facet" of Game Development on YouTube?
